newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - Mar 17.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - Mar 17.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Following the slashing of 13 per cent of the workforce in its Australian operations, Apple Computer APPL.O is to sack 4,100 workers from its 13,400-strong worldwide workforce in a A$500 million restructuring aimed at helping the company recover from financial loses - Apple is facing losses this year of A$630 million to A$1.3 billion. Page 1.

Thanks to last year's strong oil prices, some of the world's biggest oil and gas companies are planning a A$1.2 billion drilling bonanza off the coast of Australia's north-west. Lured by big discoveries in the area, Australian companies such as Woodside Petroleum And Santos Ltd have been joined by a host of international energy companies in committing to record exploration programs this year. Page 1.

As talks continue between Optus Vision partners Optus Communications, US West, Seven Network and Publishing & Broadcasting Ltd, aimed at settling legal action bought against the group by Seven, Optus Communications is negotiating to take majority control f the embattled cable TV company by buying the equity interest of PBL and Seven. Page 17

As the three-way competition between AMP, Abbey National and The Prudential in the first auction of mutual life insurer Scottish Amicable heats up, AMP has lodged its formal bid of A$4 billion for the large insurance mutual. A decision on the bids is expected to be made before the end of the month. Page 17.

Former US Secret Service agent Jim Covert, whose new company Signature Security group agreed to pay A$12 million to Tempo Services Ltd for its Securities Alarms division, says Australia is crime-ridden and needs more protection. Covert is planning to cutin on the market share of security giants Chubb and Honeywell. Page 17.

Under a deal which adds urgency to a A$200 million modernisation program planned for Comalco Ltd's Bell Bay aluminium smelter - Australia's highest cost aluminium smelter - the project is likely to continue operations until 2014. The new take-or-pay contract was signed last week with the Tasmanian Hydro Electric Commission. Page 19.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Following several seasons of stalled profits and dividends, corporate Australia has overshadowed a round of patchy December-half profits with promises of stronger growth in the second half as the curtain raiser to a sustained profit recovery for the nation's companies. Page 17.

Nine months since Prime Minister John Howard launched Optus Vision's A$3.5 billion assault on Telstra's monopoly, time is running out. In the beginning, their systems network could not cope with the volume of new hookups, and the avant-garde system is stll experiencing problems which Optus believes is near fixed. The company will begin selling local calls again next month. Page 17.

As this afternoon's deadline approaches for a resolution in the legal battle between Seven Network Ltd and its Optus Vision partners Optus Communications, US West and Publishing & Broadcasting Ltd, the parties appear no closer to delivering an acceptable eace deal. If an acceptable offer is not made to Seven and the deadline not extended, Seven can take ownership of its partners' 98 per cent of Optus Vision for between A$533 million and A$647 million. Page 17.

Speaking on the Nine Network's Business Sunday program yesterday, Coles Myer chief executive Dennis Eck said the retail giant had all but ruled out a share buyback or a break-up of the group. Despite some analysts saying a buyback could make sense, Eck said Coles was happy to invest capital in its present operations. Page 19.

RTZ-CRA technological resources group executive Ian Gould told a mining conference in Ballarat last week Australia's mining executives still need to convince the public they are responsible environmental managers at corporate, industry and individual leves and that they can offer considerable environmental expertise. Page 19.

An Australian Business Chamber/Colonial State Bank survey, which covered 502 companies in New South Wales, has revealed large manufacturers expect to shed approximately 2,300 staff in the next year, but small manufacturers will be more likely to increase staff numbers in the same period. Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Following the release of strong US retail figures, investors around the world are expecting the US Federal Reserve to lift official interest rates in an effort to contain incipient inflation. World markets are braced for the Reserve to increase rates by 5 basis points later this month, but the current uncertainty means the Australian stockmarket faces a volatile and uncertain week. Page 37.

Following a confidence-boosting interim report that was in line with forecasts, Australia's major institutional investors are predicting robust economic growth will drive company profits higher this year. Traditional cyclicals such as building materials,engineering and base metal groups are expected to be the main beneficiaries. Page 37.

Sweeping cuts announced by Heinz mean the closure or sale of at least 25 plants around the world, and the retrenchment of almost six per cent of its workforce. A spokeswoman for Heinz said yesterday there would be no change to Heinz's Australian operatios because they have already gone through significant change in the last two years. Page 37.

Following an escalation in the battle amongst the Ainsworth family shareholders, the Australian Stock Exchange is investigating a complaint by one of the seven sons of Aristocrat founder Len Ainsworth against gaming manufacturer Aristocrat Leisure, alleging a breach of the 'continuous disclosure' provisions in the Corporations Law. Page 39.

Puma Management Ltd has announced plans to launch A$879 million worth of eurobonds in London, in what is an Australian first for a private sector issuer of mortgage-backed bonds. Puma's first venture overseas, to fund Australian home loans via mortgage orginators, will allow it to diversify their source of funds, and expand their activities in the secondary mortgage market. Page 39.

Opposition parties are seeking significant changes to the retirement savings account (RSA) legislation in an effort to protect investors from a three-year bank campaign to gain direct access to superannuation through RSAs. How successful the parties are epends on the support of Independent Senator Brian Harradine and Independent Senator Mal Colston. Page 39.
THE AGE

In the biggest shakeup of its 128-year history, H.J. Heinz is planning a huge program of international restructuring that is designed to keep the company's earnings growing by at least ten per cent a year. Heinz has announced it will close or sell at leat 25 plants around the world, but a representative said yesterday there are no plans to change its Australian operations. Page B1.

While economic gains in the industrial sector were wiped out by a poor performance in the mining sector, experts believe corporate Australia is in good shape to take advantage of the predicted economic growth set to drive company profits higher in 1997. age B1.

Following waning interest in Helix Resource's Gawler Craton gold mine, the punters may latch onto Peter Topham's Mineral Commodities. A report about the latest drilling results from MinCom's White Foil discovery with French mining giant Cogema is about due, and MinCom shares have been holding at around 55 cents. Page B3.

Tap Petroleum's December half profit report of A$2.08 million is twice that forecast by the group when it floated last year. The result reflects favourable oil prices, better-than-expected oil and gas production, and mounting investor excitement over thepotential of its exploration portfolio in the Carnarvon, Australia's most prospective basin. Page B3.

Cultus Petroleum's share price continues to rise as a result of the Cornea oil discovery in the offshore Browse Basin. Cultus holds 25 per cent of the Cornea discovery and is the only listed participant, while Shell owns 50 per cent, and Chevron owns 25 er cent. Page B3.

Small businessman Tom Hall has established an electronic organiser back-up and recovery service called Phew!. The concept, which came to Hall a year ago when he lost his electronic organiser, sees him copy the data onto a floppy disc for the client to kep. Page B3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
